blocks.text: Kisi point charge ke field mein kisi point ka electric potential batane ke liye hamein aik reference (hawala) point chahiye jis ka potential zero mana jaye. Yeh point aam taur par infinity (bohat door) par liya jata hai.
Agar A ko infinity par lein aur V_A = 0 rakhein, to B ka potential V_B = W_OB/q₀ hoga, yani test charge ko infinity se B tak lane ka work ÷ charge. Subscripts hata kar:
Is ka matlab:

blocks.title: Electric potential
blocks.text: Electric field ke kisi point ka electric potential us work ke barabar hai jo aik unit positive charge ko infinity se us point tak lane mein karna parta hai, is tarah ke charge electrostatic equilibrium (tawazun) mein rahe, yani bina tez hue aahista laya jaye.

Yaad rakhein: kisi point ka potential bhi asal mein potential difference hi hai, us point aur infinity ke potential ka farq. Potential aur potential difference dono scalar quantities hain (sirf magnitude (miqdar) hota hai, direction nahi), kyunke W aur q₀ dono scalars hain.

Ab positive point charge q ke field mein kisi point ka potential nikalte hain. Iske liye unit positive charge ko infinity se us point tak (equilibrium mein) lana hai. Agar E constant hota to Eq. 16.5 ko ΔV = −E Δr ki shakal mein seedha laga dete. Lekin yahan E faasle ke square ke ulat (1/r²) badalta hai, constant nahi rehta, is liye hum basic principles (bunyadi usool) se kaam lete hain. Field radial hai (charge se seedhi lines mein bahar), Fig. 16.2.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ne Eq. (16.14) aur (16.15) mein charge q nahi likha. E = (1/4πε₀)(q/r_A r_B) rakhne se q saath aata hai: V_A − V_B = (q/4πε₀)(1/r_A − 1/r_B). Agli Eq. (16.16) mein kitab ne q likha hai, jo sahi hai.

Is se milta hai:
Aam formula: q se r faasle par electric potential V_r yeh hai:

Agar q negative ho to potential bhi negative hoga. Agar kai charges alag alag jagah par hon to har charge apna hissa deta hai, aur kisi point par kul potential sab potentials ka algebraic sum (nishan ke saath jama) hota hai. Potential scalar hai, is liye direction ka jhagra nahi, sirf + aur − ka khayal rakhein.

blocks.title: Example 16.2
blocks.problem: 5.0 × 10⁻⁸ C charge se 1.2 m door point par electric potential nikalein.
steps: Diya gaya: q = 5.0 × 10⁻⁸ C, r = 1.2 m; maloom karna hai V.
Formula: V = (1/4πε₀)(q/r), jahan 1/4πε₀ = 9 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²
Qeematen rakhein: V = (9 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²)(5.0 × 10⁻⁸ C)/1.2 m = 450/1.2 V

blocks.title: Example 16.3
blocks.problem: +8 μC aur −4 μC ke do point charges 60 cm door rakhe hain (Fig. 16.3). Charges se guzarne wali lakeer par kahan electric potential zero hoga?
steps: Potential wahan zero hoga jahan positive charge ka potential aur negative charge ka potential magnitude mein barabar hon (aik +, aik −). Positive charge bara hai, is liye aise do points hain, dono chhote negative charge ke qareeb: aik A dono charges ke darmiyan, aur aik B negative charge ke bahar (doosri taraf).
Point A ko positive charge se x faasle par lein. V = (1/4πε₀)(q/r) se:
A par positive charge ka potential = (1/4πε₀)(8×10⁻⁶ C/x)
A par negative charge ka potential = (1/4πε₀)(4×10⁻⁶ C/(60 cm − x)) (magnitude)

Dono barabar rakhein: 8/x = 4/(60 cm − x), yani 8(60 cm − x) = 4x
480 cm − 8x = 4x
12x = 480 cm
x = 40 cm
Point B negative charge se y aage hai, is liye positive charge se faasla (60 cm + y). B par positive charge ka potential = (1/4πε₀)(8×10⁻⁶ C/(60 cm + y))
B par negative charge ka potential = (1/4πε₀)(4×10⁻⁶ C/y) (magnitude)

Barabar rakhein: 8/(60 cm + y) = 4/y, yani 8y = 4(60 cm + y)
8y = 240 cm + 4y
4y = 240 cm
y = 240 cm/4
blocks.answer: x = 40 cm (A, +8 μC se 40 cm) aur y = 60 cm (B, −4 μC se 60 cm aage)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ne point B ke liye bhi A wale formulas dohra diye: positive charge ka potential (4×10⁶ C/(60 cm − x)) aur balance wali line mein x likha hai. B par sahi yeh hai: positive charge ka potential (1/4πε₀)(8×10⁻⁶ C/(60 cm + y)) aur shart (8×10⁻⁶ C)/(60 cm + y) = (4×10⁻⁶ C)/y. Is se 4(60 cm + y) = 8y aur y = 60 cm, jo kitab ka jawab hai.

blocks.alt: Aik lakeer par +8 microcoulomb aur -4 microcoulomb charges 60 cm door. Point A dono ke darmiyan, +8 se x aur -4 se (60 cm - x) faasle par. Point B -4 microcoulomb ke paar, us se y aur +8 se (60 cm + y) faasle par.
blocks.caption: Figure 16.3: 60 cm door +8 microcoulomb aur -4 microcoulomb charges, points A aur B ke saath (kitab ki Figure 16.3 ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.prompt: Example 16.3 mein kya +8 μC charge ke baen (left) taraf kahin potential zero hai? Wajah dein.
blocks.explanation: Nahi. Baen taraf har point bare +8 μC ke zyada qareeb aur chhote −4 μC se zyada door hai, is liye positive potential hamesha negative se bara rehta hai aur V kabhi zero nahi hota (sirf bohat door ja kar zero ki taraf jata hai).

blocks.text: Short summary (mukhtasar khulasa)

items: Reference: infinity par V = 0; V = W/q₀; potential scalar hai.
Point charge: V = (1/4πε₀)(q/r); negative q ke liye V negative.
Kai charges: kul potential = sab potentials ka algebraic sum.
